title: Concentric Ring Sums
description:
Given an `m x n` integer `matrix`, partition its cells into concentric rectangular rings from the outermost border inward.

Ring `0` consists of all cells on the outer border of the matrix; ring `1` consists of the outer border remaining after removing ring `0`, and so on until all cells are accounted for. Note that the innermost ring may degenerate into a single row, a single column, or a single cell.

Return an integer array `sums` where `sums[k]` is the sum of all elements in ring `k`.
hints: Maintain four shrinking boundaries: top, bottom, left, and right, just like spiral traversal.
Carefully avoid double-counting corner cells and handle the degenerate cases where top == bottom or left == right.

examples.explanation: Outer ring sums 1+2+3+6+9+8+7+4 = 40, and the single center cell forms ring 1 with sum 5.
Ring 0 contains the 10 outer border elements summing to 65; ring 1 is the inner row [6, 7] summing to 13.
A 1x4 matrix has only one ring containing all 4 elements, summing to 10.
